sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗，来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Five years ago, at the urging of federal officials, much of the United States locked down to stop the spread of COVID, a decision that over time polarized the country
sentences.zh: 五年前，在联邦官员的催促下，美国大部分地区实施了封城以遏制新冠疫情的蔓延，这一决定随着时间的推移引发了国家的分裂

sentences.en: and changed the relationship between many Americans and their government.
sentences.zh: 并改变了许多美国人与政府之间的关系。

sentences.en: Now, two prominent political scientists are making the case that there's no clear evidence that those lockdowns saved lives and that it's time for a national reckoning
sentences.zh: 现在，两位杰出的政治学家提出观点，认为没有明确证据表明这些封城拯救了生命，现在是时候进行全国性反思了

sentences.en: about the decision-making that led to those lockdowns in the first place.
sentences.zh: 反思当初导致这些封城决策的过程。

sentences.en: Today, my conversation with Stephen Macedo and Francis Lee about their new book, In COVID's Wake,
sentences.zh: 今天，我与斯蒂芬·马塞多和弗朗西斯·李就他们的新书《新冠余波》展开对话，

sentences.en: and what they say will be required for a better outcome when the next pandemic strikes.
sentences.zh: 以及他们所说当下一场大流行来袭时，要取得更好结果所必需的条件。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, March 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月20日，星期四。

sentences.en: Just to start, can I call you by your first names?
sentences.zh: 首先，我能直呼你们的名字吗？

sentences.en: Should I call you by your professional title?
sentences.zh: 我应该用你们的专业头衔称呼吗？

sentences.en: Is it okay to call you Steve and Francis?
sentences.zh: 叫你们斯蒂芬和弗朗西斯可以吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Absolutely, please.
sentences.zh: 当然，请随意。

sentences.en: Of course, now that I've called you by those names, I've pressured you into the informality.
sentences.zh: 当然，既然我都这么称呼你们了，我也就把你们推向了这种非正式的状态。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: We're actually not a show that often speaks to academics if you listen to The Daily, and that's nothing against academics.
sentences.zh: 如果你常听《每日新闻》，我们其实并不是一个经常采访学者的节目，这并不是对学者有意见。

sentences.en: We usually talk to our colleagues, but you have produced a body of work here that feels important and it feels unique.
sentences.zh: 我们通常与同行对话，但你们在这里完成了一项具有重要感和独特感的研究成果。

sentences.en: You're both tenured professors at Princeton University.
sentences.zh: 你们俩都是普林斯顿大学的终身教授。

sentences.en: Steve, you spent a lot of your career researching democracy.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬，你的职业生涯大部分时间都在研究民主。

sentences.en: Francis, your work is focused on policymaking, your big deals in your fields.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯，你的工作聚焦于决策制定，你们都是各自领域的巨擘。

sentences.en: And so to start, I want to talk about why you undertook this project of examining the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以首先，我想谈谈为什么你们要以如此严谨的方式着手审视美国

sentences.en: response to COVID in a really rigorous way.
sentences.zh: 对新冠的应对这一项目。

sentences.en: So maybe I'll just say a couple of words about that to start with.
sentences.zh: 那也许我先简单说几句来开个头。

sentences.en: I actually had started to work on a larger project on several topics on which I thought progressives were not paying enough attention to arguments coming from the other side.
sentences.zh: 我其实已经开始着手一个更大的项目，涉及几个我认为进步派没有给予足够重视、忽视了来自另一方论点的议题。

sentences.en: And that included immigration, abortion, and then COVID as well.
sentences.zh: 这包括移民、堕胎，然后还有新冠。

sentences.en: And as soon as I got deeply into it, it was clear that the COVID policy issues themselves, the COVID crisis itself, was large enough.
sentences.zh: 而当我深入研究后，很明显，新冠政策问题本身、新冠危机本身已经足够宏大。

sentences.en: And moreover, that people were not engaging in critical reflection and the sort of reckoning we've tried to do.
sentences.zh: 而且更重要的是，人们并没有进行批判性反思，也没有进行我们试图去做的这种清算。

sentences.en: So this is meant to be in part a book about policy choices, policy deliberation, and in many ways, policy mistakes perhaps that were made during COVID.
sentences.zh: 所以这既是一本关于政策选择、政策审议的书，在很多方面也是关于新冠期间可能犯下的政策错误的书。

sentences.en: But there's also a larger kind of institutional question in the background and principled question in the background, which is how did the institutions function,
sentences.zh: 但在背景中还有一个更深层的制度问题和原则问题，那就是机构是如何运作的，

sentences.en: which is supposed to be helping us to catch mistakes and correct our mistakes, to seek the truth on difficult matters.
sentences.zh: 这些机构本应帮助我们发现错误并纠正错误，在复杂问题上寻求真相。

sentences.en: How did they function under COVID?
sentences.zh: 它们在新冠期间是如何运作的？

sentences.en: And I mean, of course, journalism, science, and the academy more broadly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，包括新闻界、科学界以及更广阔的学术界。

sentences.en: And so the biggest theme that runs through the book, I think, is that these, as we call them, truth-seeking institutions did not function as well as they should have during COVID.
sentences.zh: 所以贯穿这本书的最大主题，我认为是这些我们所谓的寻真机构在新冠期间并没有发挥它们应有的作用。

sentences.en: That there was a premature policy consensus, there was an unwillingness to reexamine assumptions,
sentences.zh: 存在一种过早的政策共识，有一种不愿重新审视假设的心态，

sentences.en: and there was an intolerance of criticism and divergent points of view that emerged fairly quickly in the pandemic and that hurt us, that hurt our policy responses,
sentences.zh: 并且在疫情中相当快地出现了对批评和不同观点的极度不容忍，这伤害了我们，伤害了我们的政策应对，

sentences.en: that hurt our ability to course correct over the course of the pandemic as we learned more and had greater reason to course correct.
sentences.zh: 伤害了我们在疫情期间随着了解加深、更有理由纠错时进行路线修正的能力。

sentences.en: I mean, this was, as was frequently said at the time, a whole of government, whole of society response.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如当时经常被提及的那样，这是一场全政府、全社会的应对。

sentences.en: And it was undertaken without the normal deliberation that accompanies decision making of that degree of consequence.
sentences.zh: 而且它是在缺乏那种程度重大决策通常伴随的正常审议的情况下进行的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I mean, I remember when the pandemic began that I had some doubts as to whether these measures were going to succeed.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我的意思是，我记得疫情刚爆发时，我曾对这些措施是否会成功产生过一些怀疑。

sentences.en: I mean, it was just a normal kind of skepticism about whether government policy would work, which is, you know, sort of bedrock to political science.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这只是一种对政府政策是否会起作用的正常怀疑态度，这也是政治学的基石。

sentences.en: I mean, that is one of our main topics of inquiry, whether government policy works or whether it has unanticipated consequences.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是我们主要的探究课题之一，即政府政策是否奏效，或者它是否会产生意料之外的后果。

sentences.en: And I was so struck at the lack of skepticism over the course of the pandemic about these measures.
sentences.zh: 而我对疫情期间对这些措施缺乏怀疑态度感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: I mean, it was obvious that a large share of the workforce.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很明显，很大一部分劳动力。

sentences.en: Lack of skepticism from from some.
sentences.zh: 来自某些人的缺乏怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Yes, right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In the quarters, you know, that I travel in among academics or mainstream media, that's where there seemed to be little questioning.
sentences.zh: 在我所处的圈子里，你知道，在学者或主流媒体当中，似乎很少有人提出质疑。

sentences.en: It was almost seen as sort of wrong or immoral to raise questions about whether this was feasible for most of the population.
sentences.zh: 对这是否对大多数人可行提出质疑，几乎被视为一种错误或不道德的行为。

sentences.en: And Stephen, what was your experience of this pandemic like and how did that in any way contribute to your desire to excavate the entire thing?
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬，你对这场疫情的经历是怎样的，这在多大程度上促成了你想要彻底挖掘这一切的愿望？

sentences.en: Well, my experience was not unusual.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的经历并不特殊。

sentences.en: I was in New Jersey, a blue state, and I went along with the messaging.
sentences.zh: 我在新泽西州，这是一个蓝州，我顺从了官方的信息发布。

sentences.en: I was busy with doing other things.
sentences.zh: 我忙于做其他事情。

sentences.en: Of course, we kept teaching online and doing our research online, but I didn't really investigate skeptically during the height of COVID itself in
sentences.zh: 当然，我们继续在线上教学，在线上做研究，但在新冠高峰期的2020年、2021年，
我并没有真正带着怀疑的眼光去进行调查。

sentences.en: I started working on this book in 2022 and frankly have been kind of shocked on almost a daily basis in researching the book at the things I'm coming across and discussing with
sentences.zh: 我是在2022年开始写这本书的，坦白说，在研究这本书的过程中，我几乎每天都对所遇到并与

sentences.en: Francis.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯讨论的事情感到震惊。

sentences.en: So for me, it's been a kind of voyage of discovery, and I've been very surprised at what, you know, we've uncovered.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这是一种发现之旅，我对我们所揭露的内容感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: In your reconstruction of it, I found myself thinking, wow, I thought I knew the pandemic really well because I lived through it, but I didn't know it as well as I thought I did.
sentences.zh: 在你对它的重构中，我发现自己在想：哇，我以为我对疫情非常了解，因为我经历过它，但我对它的了解并不像我以为的那样深透。

sentences.en: And I think the biggest way many people experience the pandemic was through the mandates, right, the restrictions.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多人体验疫情最主要的方式是通过强制令，对吧，也就是各种限制措施。

sentences.en: One of the things that surprised me in your research, in your book, was that heading into the pandemic, you found that there was not a consensus that
sentences.zh: 在你的研究、你的书中，有一点让我感到惊讶：在进入疫情之初，你们发现并没有这样一种共识，即

sentences.en: these restrictions, these mandates around things like school closures, lockdowns, stay-at-home
sentences.zh: 这些限制措施、围绕学校关闭、封城、居家

sentences.en: orders, quarantining, masking, that they were the right way to try to fight a respiratory viral pandemic, that instead there was some real uncertainty about whether that made sense
sentences.zh: 令、隔离、戴口罩等强制令是应对呼吸道病毒大流行的正确方法，相反，对于这是否有意义

sentences.en: or that it could work at a large scale as public policy, and actually that there were a lot of doubts that it ever could.
sentences.zh: 或者作为公共政策能否在大规模上发挥作用，存在一些真正的动摇与不确定，事实上，很多人一直对此抱有诸多怀疑。

sentences.en: Well, there were a number of pre-COVID pandemic planning documents anticipating a respiratory pandemic such as COVID turned out to be.
sentences.zh: 好吧，有许多在新冠之前的疫情规划文件都预测了像后来新冠这样的呼吸道大流行。

sentences.en: One of them was published just in the fall of 2019, shortly before the COVID pandemic broke out.
sentences.zh: 其中一份恰好在2019年秋季出版，就在新冠疫情爆发前不久。

sentences.en: That was by the World Health
sentences.zh: 那是世界卫生

sentences.en: Organization.
sentences.zh: 组织发布的。

sentences.en: It surveyed the range of non-pharmaceutical interventions, social distancing measures, school closures.
sentences.zh: 它调查了一系列非药物干预措施、社交距离措施、学校关闭。

sentences.en: Let's just zero in on that word because we're going to use it a lot, I think.
sentences.zh: 让我们聚焦这个词，因为我认为接下来我们会经常用到它。

sentences.en: Non-pharmaceutical interventions.
sentences.zh: 非药物干预措施。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Just define that.
sentences.zh: 请定义一下。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's everything other than vaccines and drugs.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是除了疫苗和药物之外的一切。

sentences.en: The whole suite of measures from hand-washing, mask-wearing, personal hygiene, staying apart, closing schools, restricting businesses, restricting public
sentences.zh: 一整套措施，从洗手、戴口罩、个人卫生、保持距离、关闭学校、限制企业营业、限制公共

sentences.en: gatherings, not letting people go to church, and so on.
sentences.zh: 聚会、不让人去教堂等等。

sentences.en: The big things we associate with the government's response to the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我们把这些与政府应对疫情联系在一起的大事统称为此。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: Things that are often lumped under the word lockdown.
sentences.zh: 这些通常被归纳在“封城”一词之下的事情。

sentences.en: And so those measures had been contemplated before.
sentences.zh: 所以这些措施以前就被考虑过。

sentences.en: They were investigated.
sentences.zh: 它们受到过研究。

sentences.en: That was the major subject of these pre-COVID pandemic plans.
sentences.zh: 那是这些新冠前大流行计划的主要课题。

sentences.en: Obviously, getting a vaccine as soon as possible and administering it was something on which there was a consensus.
sentences.zh: 很显然，尽快获得疫苗并进行接种是各方达成共识的事情。

sentences.en: But the controversial part of the policy was the non-pharmaceutical measures.
sentences.zh: 但政策中充满争议的部分是非药物措施。

sentences.en: And what made them controversial?
sentences.zh: 是什么让它们充满争议？

sentences.en: And just how controversial were they?
sentences.zh: 而且它们的争议究竟有多大？

sentences.en: Well, they were quite controversial because one of the things that the plans emphasize is that they would be costly, that keeping children
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们相当有争议，因为这些计划强调的一点是，它们代价高昂，让儿童

sentences.en: out of school would lead to learning losses and other detriments to health and well-being, including mental well-being, from children being isolated.
sentences.zh: 远离学校会导致学习损失以及对健康和福祉的其他损害，包括因儿童被孤立而带来的心理健康问题。

sentences.en: Business closures likewise could have consequences in terms of human well-being for those who own businesses, who depend on that businesses for livelihood.
sentences.zh: 企业关闭同样会对企业主以及赖以谋生的人的人类福祉产生后果。

sentences.en: Economic loss can lead also to psychological loss and family conflicts, and so on.
sentences.zh: 经济损失也会导致心理损失和家庭冲突等等。

sentences.en: Isolating human beings who are social creatures will have a whole series of knock-on effects that the pre-pandemic planning documents discuss.
sentences.zh: 将身为社交动物的人类进行隔离，会产生一系列大流行前规划文件中讨论过的连锁反应。

sentences.en: And these matters had been studied, and they found that there was a lack of good evidence, an absence of certainty around the effectiveness of these measures.
sentences.zh: 这些问题都经过了研究，他们发现缺乏充分的证据，缺乏关于这些措施有效性的确定性。

sentences.en: Effectiveness in terms of actually stopping containing the spread of the virus.
sentences.zh: 即在真正阻止、遏制病毒传播方面的有效性。

sentences.en: Yes, especially reducing morbidity and mortality, that is to say serious illness and death.
sentences.zh: 是的，特别是减少发病率和死亡率，也就是说减少重症和死亡。

sentences.en: I'd just like to add on this 2019 World Health Organization study, the study was to examine intervention by intervention, which of them have evidence of effectiveness
sentences.zh: 我只想补充一点，关于2019年世界卫生组织的这项研究，该研究旨在逐项检查哪些干预措施有证据证明有效

sentences.en: against a respiratory pandemic.
sentences.zh: 来应对呼吸道大流行。

sentences.en: And all of the measures were rated as having very poor evidence.
sentences.zh: 而所有的措施都被评为证据非常贫乏。

sentences.en: So in other words, we don't know if these measures work.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们不知道这些措施是否管用。

sentences.en: Four of them, they recommended not to use under any circumstances.
sentences.zh: 其中四项，他们建议在任何情况下都不要使用。

sentences.en: Those four measures were quarantine of exposed persons, border closure, entry and exit screening, and contact tracing.
sentences.zh: 这四项措施是：对暴露人员进行隔离、关闭边境、出入境筛查以及接触者追踪。

sentences.en: So there were no assurances that these measures would work, but we were assured that they would have costs.
sentences.zh: 所以没有任何保证说这些措施会奏效，但我们被确信的是它们会带来代价。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And prompted by you two and what you wrote, I went and looked at this study.
sentences.zh: 在你们俩以及你们所写内容的启发下，我特意去查阅了这项研究。

sentences.en: What it says is that while there is, like you just said, low evidence, that it was plausible that these kinds of interventions could help mitigate the spread of the virus.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，虽然正如你们刚才所说，证据水平较低，但这类干预措施可能有助于缓解病毒传播，这是合乎情理的。

sentences.en: What do you make of that word plausible?
sentences.zh: 你对“合乎情理”这个词怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, they had been suggested.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们曾被提出过。

sentences.en: That's the reason why they are being studied.
sentences.zh: 这就是它们正在被研究的原因。

sentences.en: And of course, we know at some level that viruses transmit from person to person.
sentences.zh: 而且当然，我们在某种程度上知道病毒是在人与人之间传播的。

sentences.en: So one can infer that separating people from one another, putting barriers between them ought to make a difference, or that there's a logic there.
sentences.zh: 因此人们可以推断，把人与人分开、在他们之间设置屏障应该会产生影响，或者说这其中存在一种逻辑。

sentences.en: But the question is whether that could be scaled up to society or whether it would be sustainable over the course of a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但问题是这能否扩大到整个社会规模，或者它在大流行期间是否具有可持续性。

sentences.en: There was no body of evidence around that.
sentences.zh: 这方面没有任何证据基础。

sentences.en: And so when it became the mantra of the pandemic that we should follow the science,
sentences.zh: 所以当“我们应该相信科学”成为大流行的口号时，

sentences.en: there just wasn't a body of scientific work that undergirded the response that directed us to conclude that these measures were likely to be effective.
sentences.zh: 根本没有一套科学研究来支撑这种应对措施，引导我们得出这些措施可能有效的结论。

sentences.en: You're citing this WHO study, but how widespread, how dominant would you say this skepticism of these kinds of interventions as effective, as worth the cost,

sentences.en: That we direct a statewide order for people to stay at home.

sentences.en: The breaking news, stay at home.
sentences.zh: 突发新闻，待在家里。

sentences.en: And that is the order tonight from four state governors as the coronavirus pandemic spreads.

sentences.en: U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.zh: 他们只是不够信任美国人，无法从一开始就对他们坦诚相告，说类似这样的话：听着，这些干预措施，

sentences.en: they are our best guess about what's going to slow this down and save as many lives as possible and get us through this pandemic in the best shape that we possibly can.
sentences.zh: 它们是我们对如何减缓疫情、拯救尽可能多的生命以及以最佳状态度过这场大流行的最好猜测。

sentences.en: And to say, essentially, this is a large-scale experiment, and we have to be honest, it's going to involve all these tradeoffs, economic, social, academic, psychological.

sentences.en: I mean, that is admittedly a hard message to ask people to join you.

sentences.en: I think under the pressure of the crisis, the public demanding action with the sense of catastrophe unfolding, I think they indulged in a great deal of wishful thinking.

sentences.en: And so when advocates of non-pharmaceutical interventions recommended these measures and were optimistic about it, they heard what they wanted to hear.

sentences.en: I mean, there was a sense that, with the two weeks to slow the spread, that, you know, we get control of this thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一种感觉，通过两周的减缓传播，你知道的，我们就能控制住这个东西。

sentences.en: You know, that it'll go up, there'll be a peak, and then it'll come down, we'll defeat it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它会上升，会出现一个峰值，然后会下降，我们会战胜它。

sentences.en: This will be done in a few months.
sentences.zh: 这一切将在几个月内完成。

sentences.en: So there was optimism that this could be over with in short order.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们乐观地认为，这可以在短时间内结束。

sentences.en: But there just wasn't a lot of long-term thinking of any sort around this, and a great deal of hope that long-term, these measures wouldn't be in place.
sentences.zh: 但围绕这一点并没有进行太多任何形式的长期思考，并且人们抱有极大希望，即从长远来看，这些措施不会一直实施下去。

sentences.en: I mean, I think there was a general social fixation on the number of deaths, the spread of cases.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为社会普遍痴迷于死亡人数和病例的传播。

sentences.en: We developed a kind of tunnel vision of the one indice that public health officials were focusing on was sickness and death from COVID.

sentences.en: And these other matters were not highlighted by political leaders or by public health officials.
sentences.zh: 而政治领导人或公共卫生官员并没有强调这些其他问题。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我猜归纳我的问题，对拯救生命进行单一的深入关注是可以的吗？

sentences.en: I don't see how it is if there are significant costs involved, including in the currency of life.
sentences.zh: 我不明白如果涉及巨大的代价（包括生命的代价），这怎么可以。

sentences.en: These policy choices always involve a variety of values, and we have to not simply focus on the one indice of saving lives, I think, insofar as—
sentences.zh: 这些政策选择总是涉及各种价值观，我认为，我们不能仅仅关注拯救生命这一个指标，只要——

sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.zh: 请解释一下，因为我认为会有一些听众说，在大流行中，这才是唯一重要的指标。

sentences.en: You know, look, early on, I think that the initial lockdown orders and those conditions of uncertainty and so on may have made some sense.
sentences.zh: 你知道，听着，在早期，我认为最初的封锁令和这些不确定性等条件可能是有一定道理的。

sentences.en: but we learned things over the summer that should have helped inform the strategy and that should have at least been more vigorously debated.
sentences.zh: 但我们在夏天了解到的情况本应该有助于塑造策略，并且至少应该得到更激进的辩论。

sentences.en: The success of the public health measures always depended upon public buy-in, public willingness to comply, a public willingness to trust and to go along.
sentences.zh: 公共卫生措施的成功始终取决于公众的买账、公众配合的意愿、公众信任和随大流的意愿。

sentences.en: And there wasn't enough public deliberation about these matters.
sentences.zh: 对这些事情没有进行足够的公众审议。

sentences.en: Too much power was accorded to narrow experts in public health and epidemiology in particular.
sentences.zh: 过多的权力被赋予了公共卫生领域的狭隘专家，特别是流行病学专家。

sentences.en: There should have been a wider conversation simply involving many more people with broader expertise, but it also should have involved ordinary people in the public who, after all,

sentences.en: were being the ones asked to make sacrifices in their own lives, to adopt policies which always involve trade-offs across values, risks,
sentences.zh: 他们是那些被要求在自己的生活中做出牺牲、采纳政策的人，这些政策总是涉及不同价值观、风险之间的权衡，

sentences.en: how much are we willing to give up to not visit an elderly relative in the hospital, to not have a funeral, to not be allowed to attend church on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 为了不探望住院的老年亲属、不举行葬礼、不被允许在周日去教堂，我们愿意放弃多少。

sentences.en: These sorts of public questions don't have scientific answers.
sentences.zh: 这类公共问题没有科学答案。

sentences.en: They're value judgments about which ordinary people have a certain expertise about their own lives and what matters to them.
sentences.zh: 它们是价值判断，普通人对自己的生活以及对他们重要的事情拥有一定的专业知识。

sentences.en: And they should have been involved as well in the deliberation about these measures.
sentences.zh: 他们也本应参与到对这些措施的审议中。

sentences.en: I would also add on this point that it's not just that there were costs.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点，不仅是存在代价。

sentences.zh: 而是代价分配不公，导致一些人为保护他人的生命而遭受苦难。

sentences.en: I mean, the pandemic restrictions did not protect essential workers from exposure to COVID.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大流行限制并没有保护基本工作者免受新冠暴露。

sentences.en: And so they were being asked to bear the societal burden of disease.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们被要求承担疾病的社会负担。

sentences.en: So I think we have to confront the nature of these restrictions, that it's not a matter of saving everyone's life.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们必须正视这些限制的性质，这并非拯救所有人的生命的问题。

sentences.en: It was saving some.
sentences.zh: 这是拯救一部分人。

sentences.en: I mean, that was all they could have achieved, is to save some.

sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都创作“拼写蜜蜂”（Spelling Bee）和“字母箱”（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你刚才听到的人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 从今天开始游玩。

sentences.en: The coronavirus pandemic has left a trail of destruction in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 冠状病毒大流行在美国

sentences.en: and around the world.
sentences.zh: 和世界各地留下了毁灭的轨迹。

sentences.en: I've never seen so much death.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过这么多的死亡。

sentences.en: So many of the patients are dying, despite our best efforts.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们尽了最大努力，还是有这么多的患者在死去。

sentences.en: I am fighting two wars.
sentences.zh: 我在打两场战争。

sentences.en: I'm fighting a war against coronavirus, and I'm fighting a war against stupidity.
sentences.zh: 我在打一场抗击冠状病毒的战争，我还在打一场对抗愚昧的战争。

sentences.en: People are not listening to what we're saying.
sentences.zh: 人们不听我们在说什么。

sentences.en: Protesters say the shutdown has lasted too long and inflicted too much pain, especially on small businesses.
sentences.zh: 抗议者表示，停摆持续的时间太长，造成了太多的痛苦，特别是对小企业而言。

sentences.en: The cure can now be worse than the disease.
sentences.zh: 现在解药可能比疾病本身更糟糕。

sentences.en: There are 30 million people that are out of work in this country.
sentences.zh: 这个国家有3000万人失业。

sentences.en: We have to go back to work.
sentences.zh: 我们必须回去工作。

sentences.en: Open our country.
sentences.zh: 开放我们的国家。

sentences.en: Open us up.
sentences.zh: 解封吧。

sentences.en: We need to work.
sentences.zh: 我们需要工作。

sentences.en: We are ordering you.
sentences.zh: 我们在命令你们。

sentences.en: End the shutdown now.
sentences.zh: 立刻结束停摆。

sentences.en: Now 36 states are seeing increases in new weekly infections this morning.
sentences.zh: 现在，36个州的每周新增感染人数在今天上午呈现上升趋势。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: just suffered the deadliest day of the summer so far.
sentences.zh: 刚刚遭遇了入夏以来最致命的一天。

sentences.en: We want to reopen the schools.
sentences.zh: 我们想要重新开放学校。

sentences.en: Everybody wants it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想要。

sentences.en: The moms want it.
sentences.zh: 妈妈们想要。

sentences.en: The dads want it.
sentences.zh: 爸爸们想要。

sentences.en: The kids want it.
sentences.zh: 孩子们想要。

sentences.en: It's time to do it.
sentences.zh: 是时候这么做了。

sentences.en: Tonight, with the virus raging and hospitals on the brink, the president putting pressure on schools,
sentences.zh: 今晚，随着病毒肆虐和医院濒临崩溃，总统向学校施压，

sentences.en: today threatening to cut off funding for districts that don't reopen in person.
sentences.zh: 今天威胁要切断对不进行线下复课的学区的资金支持。

sentences.en: Many teachers across the country are pushing back on plans to bring students back into the classroom.
sentences.zh: 全国许多教师都在抵制让学生重返课堂的计划。

sentences.en: This COVID-19 world we've been living in has lasted a full six months.
sentences.zh: 我们一直生活其中的这个COVID-19世界已经持续了整整六个月。

sentences.en: The official COVID-19 death toll in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国官方的COVID-19死亡人数

sentences.en: has now surpassed 200,000, the most of any nation.
sentences.zh: 现已突破20万，是所有国家中最高的。

sentences.en: It's a little shocking to see so many people not wearing protective masks, not staying six feet apart.
sentences.zh: 看到这么多人不戴防护口罩，不保持六英尺的距离，有点令人震惊。

sentences.en: It's a hoax!
sentences.zh: 这是骗局！

sentences.en: It's a hoax!
sentences.zh: 这是骗局！

sentences.en: How can we coexist with anti-science people?
sentences.zh: 我们如何能与反科学的人共存？

sentences.en: What can we do to survive the ignorance?
sentences.zh: 我们能做些什么来在无知中生存？

sentences.en: I just think we need to hunker down and get through this fall and winter because it's not going to be easy.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得我们需要咬紧牙关度过今年秋冬，因为这不会容易。

sentences.en: Let's talk about what happens as the pandemic progresses and the impacts and the cost of these shutdowns, these quarantines,
sentences.zh: 让我们来谈谈随着大流行进展会发生什么，以及这些停摆、这些隔离的影响和代价，

sentences.en: these stay-at-home orders that the government told us we needed, they begin to grow.
sentences.zh: 政府告诉我们需要的这些居家令，开始不断增加。

sentences.en: You, too, posit that even as those costs are rising, the country's public health officials show very little tolerance for an open debate about whether this approach should change.
sentences.zh: 你们两人也提出，即使这些代价在不断上升，国家的公共卫生官员对是否应该改变这种做法展开公开辩论表现出极小的容忍度。

sentences.en: And for you, this is encapsulated by what happens to three well-known scientists who decide to write what becomes known as the Great Barrington Declaration,
sentences.zh: 对你们来说，这由三位决定撰写后来被称为《大巴灵顿宣言》的知名科学家的遭遇所概括，

sentences.en: which arrives in the fall of 2020, so about seven months into the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 该宣言于2020年秋季发表，大约是在大流行开始七个月后。

sentences.en: Can you lay out what that declaration was and how the conversation in response to it unfolded?
sentences.zh: 你能阐述一下那份宣言是什么，以及随之展开的对话是如何进行的吗？

sentences.en: Well, they were three scientists from Stanford University, Harvard University, and Oxford, well-known, well-established scientists with excellent publication records.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们是来自斯坦福大学、哈佛大学和牛津大学的三位科学家，是知名、老牌的科学家，拥有优秀的发表记录。

sentences.en: They were concerned about the costs of the closures.
sentences.zh: 他们担心关闭带来的代价。

sentences.en: They were concerned about the disproportionate burdens being borne by essential workers and schoolchildren.
sentences.zh: 他们担心基本工作者和学龄儿童正在承受的不成比例的负担。

sentences.en: and they attempted to start a conversation.
sentences.zh: 他们试图发起对话。

sentences.en: They were arguing that rather than keeping the whole of society closed, rather than keeping schools closed for children at very little risk from COVID,
sentences.zh: 他们当时认为，与其让整个社会处于封锁状态，与其让面临新冠风险极小的儿童学校关闭，

sentences.en: we should be focusing protection on the vulnerable parts of the population.
sentences.zh: 我们应该将保护重点放在人口中的脆弱群体上。

sentences.en: And by October 4th, when that document was published, we had good evidence to suggest to know that there was highly uneven vulnerability
sentences.zh: 到 10 月 4 日该文件发布时，我们已经有充分的证据表明，不同人群的脆弱程度极不均衡，

sentences.en: across the population, age being the principal factor.
sentences.zh: 年龄是其中最主要的因素。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Death rates among the elderly were orders of magnitude larger than the general population.
sentences.zh: 老年人的死亡率比普通人口高出几个数量级。

sentences.en: Much, much higher.
sentences.zh: 高得多，高得多。

sentences.en: And what they suggested was focusing protection on the vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 他们的建议是将保护重点放在弱势群体身上。

sentences.en: And how did they suggest doing that?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么建议这样做的呢？

sentences.en: The Great Barrington Declaration is a strategic plan.
sentences.zh: 《大巴灵顿宣言》是一个战略计划。

sentences.en: I mean, it's one page long, and it just lays out a different approach.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它只有一页纸，只是提出了另一种方法。

sentences.en: And then it invites people to think carefully about how it might be implemented, how one might engage in the effort of protecting the vulnerable,
sentences.zh: 然后它邀请人们认真思考如何实施这一计划，如何参与保护弱势群体的行动，

sentences.en: like more COVID testing of people who interact with the elderly, more help, you know, organized society-wide help of, you know, getting groceries and taking them to the elderly.
sentences.zh: 例如对与老人接触的人进行更多的新冠检测，提供更多帮助，你知道的，在全社会范围内组织帮助，比如去杂货店采购并把东西送到老人手中。

sentences.en: Like, you know, looking for ways to reduce the risk of those who were at most risk of severe outcomes.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，寻找方法来降低那些最容易面临严重后果的人群的风险。

sentences.en: That was what they hoped to initiate with the Great Barrington Declaration, was then a discussion that might develop more fully paths to implementing this strategic plan.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们希望通过《大巴灵顿宣言》开启的目标，随后是一场可能更全面地发展实施这一战略计划路径的讨论。

sentences.en: But instead, they were denounced.
sentences.zh: 但相反，他们遭到了一致谴责。

sentences.en: They were presented as if they wanted people to die.
sentences.zh: 他们被描述成似乎希望人们去死一样。

sentences.en: You know, their motives were profoundly questioned.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们的动机受到了极大的质疑。

sentences.en: And that happened also at the highest levels of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这种情况也发生在美国

sentences.en: scientific establishment.
sentences.zh: 科学界的最高层。

sentences.en: Just explain that.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下这一点。

sentences.en: Well, it's when the declaration came out a few days later, the great band of people were charged with adopting a herd immunity strategy to let the virus rip through the population.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就在宣言发表几天后，这群人被指控采取群体免疫策略，任由病毒在人群中肆虐。

sentences.en: And that would cost hundreds of thousands of lives.
sentences.zh: 那将付出数十万人的生命代价。

sentences.en: We have now the email by Francis Collins, the head of the National Institutes of Health, in effect, Dr. Anthony Fauci's boss.
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到了美国国立卫生研究院负责人、实际上是安东尼·福奇博士的上司弗朗西斯·柯林斯的电子邮件。

sentences.en: He said in his email to Dr. Fauci and others, the document from the three fringe epidemiologists is getting a lot of attention.
sentences.zh: 他在给福奇博士和其他人的电子邮件中说，这三位边缘流行病学家的文件正受到极大的关注。

sentences.en: Even a co-signature from a Nobel Prize winner, people were signing this declaration online.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一位诺贝尔奖得主的联署，人们正在网上签署这份宣言。

sentences.en: And he said there needs to be a quick and devastating takedown.
sentences.zh: 他说，必须进行一次迅速而具有毁灭性的打击。

sentences.en: For those of you who don't know, the Great Barrington Declaration is a awful, awful idea.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不知道的人来说，《大巴灵顿宣言》是一个糟糕透顶的主意。

sentences.en: It's the fantasy of petulant children who just want this pandemic to be over.
sentences.zh: 这只是一些急躁的孩子们的幻想，他们只是希望这场大流行赶紧结束。

sentences.en: And it is appalling, really, that experts would even suggest something like this as a real plan.
sentences.zh: 专家们甚至会把这样的话题当作真正的计划提出来，这实在令人震惊。

sentences.en: Critics, including the director general of the World Health Organization, call this plan a dangerous approach and not an option.
sentences.zh: 包括世界卫生组织总干事在内的批评人士称这一计划是一种危险的方法，根本不可行。

sentences.en: You're essentially asking people to go to concentration camps.
sentences.zh: 你这基本上是要求人们去集中营。

sentences.en: I mean, that's an overstatement, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点夸大其词了，对不起。

sentences.en: But separating the families, it's, you know, it's just not workable.
sentences.zh: 但是把家庭拆散，你知道的，这根本行不通。

sentences.en: NIH director Francis Collins said this, well, what I worry about with this is it's being presented as if it's a major alternative view
sentences.zh: 美国国立卫生研究院（NIH）主任弗朗西斯·柯林斯这样说道，嗯，我对此感到担心的是，它被表现得好像是一个重大且另类的观点，

sentences.en: that's held by large numbers of experts in the scientific community.
sentences.zh: 得到了科学界大量专家的支持。

sentences.en: That is not true.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: This is a fringe component of epidemiology.
sentences.zh: 这是流行病学中的一个边缘成分。

sentences.en: This is not mainstream science.
sentences.zh: 这不是主流科学。

sentences.en: It is dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这是危险的。

sentences.en: If you let infections rip, as it were, and say, let everybody get infected that's going to be able to be getting infected, and then we'll have herd immunity.
sentences.zh: 如果你任由感染蔓延，可以说，让所有能够被感染的人都感染，然后我们就会获得群体免疫。

sentences.en: Quite frankly, that is nonsense.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，这纯属无稽之谈。

sentences.en: Francis, was there something to the backlash kind of unprincipled?
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯，这种强烈的反对有什么不讲道理的地方吗？

sentences.en: Because I recall that there was a response from the scientific and public health community that basically amounted to this alternative vision,
sentences.zh: 因为我记得科学界和公共卫生界做出的回应，基本上等于说这种替代愿景——

sentences.en: the Great Parenting Declaration, it's just not practical.
sentences.zh: 《大巴灵顿宣言》，根本不切实际。

sentences.en: You know, how do you separate vulnerable people from the rest of society?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你如何把弱势群体和社会的其余部分隔离开来？

sentences.en: Think about your immunocompromised grandmother.
sentences.zh: 想想你那位免疫力低下的祖母。

sentences.en: She lives on the third floor of a multigenerational household.
sentences.zh: 她住在多代同堂家庭的第三层。

sentences.en: How is she supposed to be protected when everybody else is suddenly liberated from their stay-at-home orders
sentences.zh: 当其他所有人突然都不受居家令限制时，她怎么可能得到保护呢？

sentences.en: and bringing that virus home to then infect her, who is very, very vulnerable?
sentences.zh: 而这些人会把病毒带回家，进而传染给她这个极其脆弱的人。

sentences.en: Well, the question presupposes that the measures that we were taking were working.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个问题的前提是假设我们采取的措施正在发挥作用。

sentences.en: They were not protecting the essential workers.
sentences.zh: 它们并没有保护好基层必要岗位的员工。

sentences.en: And if we're not going to be able to contain the virus, if it's going to continue to spread through society, if it's going to become endemic,
sentences.zh: 如果我们无法控制病毒，如果它继续在社会中传播，如果它将变成地方性流行病，

sentences.en: then aiming at protecting those at most risk makes more sense.
sentences.zh: 那么把目标对准保护那些风险最高的人群就更有意义了。

sentences.en: It's a matter of what you see as the future trajectory here.
sentences.zh: 这是一个如何看待未来发展轨迹的问题。

sentences.en: So the question of what the approach should be to COVID, of course, ends up in the hands of states and governors.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于应对新冠的方法应该是什么的问题，最终自然落在了各州和州长手中。

sentences.en: And as all our listeners will remember, states take very divergent approaches.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所有的听众所记得的那样，各州采取了截然不同的方法。

sentences.en: So talk to us about what you find in your research about that breakdown across the 50 states, especially on the metric of saving lives.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲你在研究中发现的关于这 50 个州之间差异的情况，特别是在拯救生命这一衡量标准上。

sentences.en: So at the outset, states across the board implemented stay-at-home orders.
sentences.zh: 因此，一开始，各州全面实施了居家令。

sentences.en: 43 states put them in place.
sentences.zh: 43 个州落实了这一政策。

sentences.en: Of the seven states that did not, all but one had broad business closures.
sentences.zh: 在没有落实的 7 个州中，除了一个州外，其余都广泛关闭了企业。

sentences.en: So there was great unity of response across the country, and these measures were hugely popular.
sentences.zh: 因此全国各地的应对措施高度一致，这些措施极其受欢迎。

sentences.en: Something like 87% of Americans supported the measures at the time of their implementation.
sentences.zh: 在实施时，大约有 87% 的美国人支持这些措施。

sentences.en: Where we began to see policy divergence is in the reopening process.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到政策分歧的地方是在重新开放的过程中。

sentences.en: Democratic-leaning states maintained these stay-at-home orders two and a half times longer than Republican-leaning states.
sentences.zh: 民主党倾向的州维持居家令的时间是共和党倾向的州的 2.5 倍。

sentences.en: Democratic-leaning states were slower to reopen schools, dramatically slower to reopen schools.
sentences.zh: 民主党倾向的州重新开放学校的速度较慢，慢得惊人。

sentences.en: They maintained more stringent restrictions in terms of, you know, business closures and which businesses could reopen and when and on what timeline and
sentences.zh: 他们在以下方面维持了更严格的限制，你知道的，比如关闭企业、哪些企业可以重新开放、何时开放、按什么时间表，以及

sentences.en: whether you'd have to have outdoor dining or whether restaurants would be closed again in winter of 2020.
sentences.zh: 你是否必须在户外用餐，或者餐馆是否会在 2020 年冬天再次关闭。

sentences.en: So there were substantial policy differences between red states and blue states over the course of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 因此，在大流行期间，红州和蓝州之间存在着实质性的政策差异。

sentences.en: And at the time that the vaccine rollout began, there was no difference between red states and blue states in their cumulative COVID mortality over the course of the crisis.
sentences.zh: 在疫苗开始推广的时候，红州和蓝州在整场危机期间的累计新冠死亡率上没有任何区别。

sentences.en: No difference.
sentences.zh: 没有区别。

sentences.en: No difference.
sentences.zh: 没有区别。

sentences.en: The difference begins to emerge in the post-vaccine period.
sentences.zh: 这种差异开始在疫苗接种后时期显现出来。

sentences.en: And that's where you begin to see blue states faring better than red states.
sentences.zh: 也就是从那时起，你开始看到蓝州的情况比红州要好。

sentences.en: So that by the end of the time series we examine in our book, which stops in January 23, Republican states had 30 percent more COVID mortality than Democratic states.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们书中研究的时间序列结束时（即 2023 年 1 月停止），共和党州的新冠死亡率比民主党州高出 30%。

sentences.en: Can I ask you to linger on this period before the vaccines?
sentences.zh: 我能请你多关注一下疫苗出现之前的这段时期吗？

sentences.en: Because from what you're saying, Francis, before the vaccines were introduced, states that had more and longer restrictive measures had the same
sentences.zh: 因为从你的说法来看，弗朗西斯，在疫苗推出之前，采取更多、更久限制措施的州，其死亡人数

sentences.en: more or less number of deaths as states that had less and shorter restrictive measures.
sentences.zh: 与采取较少、较短限制措施的州的死亡人数差不多。

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is what we can see as we look back.
sentences.zh: 当我们回首往事时，我们就能看到这一点。

sentences.en: We can see that there was a great deal of variation in how states responded, but that variation doesn't correlate with variation in
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到，各州的应对方式存在很大的差异，但这种差异与向疾控中心报告的该疾病死亡率所衡量的新冠结果差异并不相关。

sentences.en: COVID outcomes as measured by mortality from the disease as reported to the CDC.
sentences.zh: 并且我们控制了诸如州人口年龄结构、肥胖比例、

sentences.en: And we control for factors like the age structure of the state population, the percent with obesity, the percent
